verses.text: The song of songs (the greatest song), which is Solomon's.
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth. For your love is better than wine.
Because of the savour (smell) of your good ointments (perfumes), your name is as ointment (perfume) poured forth (out). Therefore do the virgins love you.
Draw me, we will run after you. The king has brought me into his chambers (rooms). We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will remember your love more than wine. The upright (good people) love you.
I am black, but comely (lovely), O you daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun has looked upon me (darkened my skin). My mother's children were angry with me. They made me the keeper of the vineyards. But my own vineyard have I not kept.
Tell me, O you whom my soul loves, where you feed (your flock), where you make your flock to rest at noon. For why should I be as one that turns aside by the flocks of your companions (friends)?
If you know not, O you fairest (most beautiful) among women, go your way forth (out) by the footsteps of the flock, and feed your kids (young goats) beside the shepherds' tents.
I have compared you, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks are comely (lovely) with rows of jewels, your neck with chains of gold.
We will make you borders (chains) of gold with studs (spots) of silver.
While the king sits at his table, my spikenard (costly perfume) sends forth (out) the smell of it.
A bundle of myrrh (sweet-smelling spice) is my wellbeloved (dear love) to me. He shall lie all night betwixt (between) my breasts.
My beloved is to me as a cluster of camphire (henna flowers) in the vineyards of Engedi.
Look, you are fair (beautiful), my love. Look, you are fair (beautiful). You have doves' eyes.
Look, you are fair (handsome), my beloved, yes, pleasant. Also our bed is green.
The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.

verses.text: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.
As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
As the apple tree among the trees of the wood (forest), so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
He brought me to the banqueting house (house of feasting), and his banner over me was love.
Stay (strengthen) me with flagons (raisin cakes), comfort me with apples. For I am sick of love (weak with love).
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand does embrace (hold) me.
I charge you (make you promise), O you daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes (gazelles), and by the hinds (female deer) of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
The voice of my beloved! Look, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
My beloved is like a roe (gazelle) or a young hart (deer). Look, he stands behind our wall, he looks forth (out) at the windows, showing himself through the lattice (window screen).
My beloved spoke, and said to me: Rise up, my love, my fair (beautiful) one, and come away.
For, lo (look), the winter is past, the rain is over and gone.
The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle (turtledove) is heard in our land.
The fig tree puts forth (out) her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise (get up), my love, my fair (beautiful) one, and come away.

O my dove, that are in the clefts (cracks) of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs (steep cliffs), let me see your countenance (face), let me hear your voice. For sweet is your voice, and your countenance (face) is comely (lovely).
Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines. For our vines have tender grapes.
My beloved is mine, and I am his. He feeds among the lilies.
Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe (gazelle) or a young hart (deer) upon the mountains of Bether.

verses.text: By night on my bed I sought (looked for) him whom my soul loves. I sought (looked for) him, but I found him not.
I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek (look for) him whom my soul loves. I sought (looked for) him, but I found him not.
The watchmen (guards) that go about the city found me, to whom I said: Did you see him whom my soul loves?

It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber (room) of her that conceived (gave birth to) me.
I charge you (make you promise), O you daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes (gazelles), and by the hinds (female deer) of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

Who is this that comes out of the wilderness (desert) like pillars (columns) of smoke, perfumed with myrrh (sweet-smelling spice) and frankincense (sweet-smelling tree gum), with all powders of the merchant?
Look, his bed, which is Solomon's. 60 valiant (brave) men are about it, of the valiant (brave) of Israel.
They all hold swords, being expert in war. Every man has his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.
King Solomon made himself a chariot (carried chair) of the wood of Lebanon.
He made the pillars (posts) of it of silver, the bottom of it of gold, the covering of it of purple, the middle of it being paved (decorated) with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

Go forth (out), O you daughters of Zion, and behold (see) king Solomon with the crown with which his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals (wedding), and in the day of the gladness of his heart.

4.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase and added speaker labels that are not in the KJV), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Look, you are fair (beautiful), my love. Look, you are fair (beautiful). You have doves' eyes within your locks (hair). Your hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn (freshly sheared), which came up from the washing, of which every one bear twins, and none is barren (without young) among them.
Your lips are like a thread of scarlet (bright red), and your speech is comely (lovely). Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within your locks (hair).
Your neck is like the tower of David builded (built) for an armoury (place for weapons), on which there hang 1,000 bucklers (shields), all shields of mighty men.
Your 2 breasts are like 2 young roes (gazelles) that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh (sweet-smelling spice), and to the hill of frankincense (sweet-smelling tree gum).
You are all fair (beautiful), my love. There is no spot in you.
Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse (bride), with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
You have ravished (captured) my heart, my sister, my spouse (bride). You have ravished (captured) my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
How fair (beautiful) is your love, my sister, my spouse (bride)! How much better is your love than wine! And the smell of your ointments (perfumes) than all spices!
Your lips, O my spouse (bride), drop as the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. And the smell of your garments (clothes) is like the smell of Lebanon.
A garden inclosed (with a wall around it) is my sister, my spouse (bride), a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits, camphire (henna flowers), with spikenard (costly perfume),
Spikenard (costly perfume) and saffron, calamus (sweet cane) and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense (sweet-smelling tree gum), myrrh (sweet-smelling spice) and aloes, with all the chief spices.
A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.
Awake, O north wind, and come, you south. Blow upon my garden, so that the spices of it may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.

verses.text: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse (bride). I have gathered my myrrh (sweet-smelling spice) with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey. I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends. Drink, yes, drink abundantly (plenty), O beloved.

I sleep, but my heart wakes. It is the voice of my beloved that knocks, saying: Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled (pure one). For my head is filled with dew, and my locks (hair) with the drops of the night.
I have put off my coat. How shall I put it on? I have washed my feet. How shall I defile (dirty) them?
My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels (heart) were moved for him.
I rose up to open to my beloved. And my hands dropped with myrrh (sweet-smelling spice), and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
I opened to my beloved. But my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone. My soul failed when he spoke. I sought (looked for) him, but I could not find him. I called him, but he gave me no answer.
The watchmen (guards) that went about the city found me, they smote (struck) me, they wounded me. The keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
I charge you (make you promise), O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am sick of love (weak with love).
What is your beloved more than another beloved, O you fairest (most beautiful) among women? What is your beloved more than another beloved, that you do so charge us (make us promise)?
My beloved is white and ruddy (healthy red), the chiefest among 10,000.
His head is as the most fine gold. His locks (hair) are bushy (wavy), and black as a raven.
His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set (well placed).
His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers. His lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh (sweet-smelling spice).
His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl (a precious stone). His belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.
His legs are as pillars (columns) of marble, set upon sockets (bases) of fine gold. His countenance (appearance) is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
His mouth is most sweet. Yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

verses.text: Where is your beloved gone, O you fairest (most beautiful) among women? Where is your beloved turned aside, so that we may seek (look for) him with you?
My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine. He feeds among the lilies.
You are beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely (lovely) as Jerusalem, terrible (awesome) as an army with banners (flags).
Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.
Your teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, of which every one bears twins, and there is not one barren (without young) among them.
As a piece of a pomegranate are your temples within your locks (hair).
There are 60 queens, and 80 concubines (second wives), and virgins without number.

My dove, my undefiled (pure one) is but one. She is the only one of her mother, she is the choice (favorite) one of her that bare (gave birth to) her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her. Yes, the queens and the concubines (second wives), and they praised her.
Who is she that looks forth (out) as the morning, fair (beautiful) as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible (awesome) as an army with banners (flags)?
I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished (bloomed), and the pomegranates budded.
Or ever I was aware (before I knew it), my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib (a noble people).
Return, return, O Shulamite (woman of Shulam). Return, return, so that we may look upon you. What will you see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.

verses.text: How beautiful are your feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! The joints of your thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning (skillful) workman.
Your navel is like a round goblet (cup), which wants not liquor (never lacks drink). Your belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.
Your 2 breasts are like 2 young roes (gazelles) that are twins.
Your neck is as a tower of ivory. Your eyes like the fishpools (pools) in Heshbon, by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
Your head upon you is like Carmel, and the hair of your head like purple. The king is held in the galleries (captured by your hair).
How fair (beautiful) and how pleasant are you, O love, for delights!
This your stature (height) is like to a palm tree, and your breasts to clusters of grapes.
I said: I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs (branches) of it. Now also your breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of your nose like apples,
And the roof of your mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goes down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.
I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me.
Come, my beloved, let us go forth (out) into the field. Let us lodge (stay) in the villages.
Let us get up early to the vineyards. Let us see if the vine flourish (bloom), whether the tender grape appear, and the pomegranates bud forth (out). There will I give you my loves.
The mandrakes (a sweet-smelling plant) give a smell, and at our gates are all manner of pleasant fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for you, O my beloved.
